title: Architecture
subject: gated-scoped-ac
summary: Which file of the library owns which concern, how long each piece lives, and how one request passes from the access context to a query.

axioms.text: The engine is pure: it reads config and the bag and returns a [[scope]] or a verdict. It builds drizzle SQL fragments and never holds a connection.
The gate is the only module that touches the database handle, and its read, update and delete each require a scope of the matching entity and action.
Only the engine can mint a scope: the brand symbol is declared in `engine.ts` and exported nowhere.
Config is validated when it loads and when the engine is built. A request never meets a malformed rule.

purpose.intro: The library is two parts with nothing between them that could decide: an engine that resolves and a [[gated db]] that executes. This page maps the files to those parts and follows one request through them.

reference.statement: One file per concern, all under `src/`.

snippets.code:
shared/libs/gated-scoped-ac/src/
├── index.ts          the public surface (the brand symbol is not on it)
├── engine.ts         createAc: permissions + bag → Scope / Verdict; role → permission resolution; the brand
├── gate.ts           createGatedDb: runs a Scope against the raw handle; gateDb(bag), gateDb.ungated()
├── dsl.ts            the rule types: Action, Operand, Condition, Traversal, AccessRule, Permission, RoleNode
├── config.ts         definePermissions, registerPermissions, registerForests, impliedRoles
├── context.ts        ScopedAcRequestContext, ScopedAcBag: the per-request access context
├── visibility.ts     PUBLIC / PRIVATE and isPrivate
├── validate.ts       the ConfigValidator port and assertNoIssues
└── adapters/
    └── zod.ts        zodConfigValidator, exported as @libs/gated-scoped-ac/zod

reference.statement: The imports run one way: the engine never depends on config, and only the adapter knows zod.

claims.text: `engine.ts` imports the DSL types and drizzle-orm, and no config. `config.ts` can therefore import the DSL types without a cycle.
`gate.ts` imports the engine's types and drizzle-orm. It calls the engine only through the injected `engine.allowCreate`, for the one write that has no scope to require.
`config.ts` imports `dsl.ts` and `validate.ts`. It holds no schema, so the check that needs a column (an `is` against an array or json column) runs in `createAc`, once, when the engine is built.
`context.ts` imports only the gate's and engine's types. Nothing under `src/` imports zod except `adapters/zod.ts`.

reference.statement: The engine and the gate factory hold config, tables and a handle, and nothing that belongs to a request.

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Piece | Built | Lives for |
|---|---|---|
| permission map, role list | when the config module loads (`registerPermissions`, `registerForests`) | the process |
| engine | once, at app boot (`createAc`) | the process |
| gate factory | once per database handle, at app boot (`createGatedDb`) | the process |
| access context: bag, roles, permissions | once per request, by the app's hydration middleware | the request |
| `gateDb(bag)` | per request; hydration puts one on the context | the request |
| `Scope`, `Verdict` | per call to the engine | the call |

reference.statement: Roles become permissions once, in hydration. Everything after it takes permissions, and the engine never sees a role at request time.

snippets.code:
session middleware verifies the caller
  └─ hydration builds the bag, unions the baseline roles with the active membership's,
     engine.resolveEffectivePermissions(roles, bag) → permissions
     gatedDb(bag)                                   → gateDb
       └─ stores { bag, roles, permissions, gateDb } as `scopedAc`
            │
            ▼
  read     service     engine.resolveRead(permissions, "meteor", bag)          → Scope<"meteor", "read">
           repository  gateDb.read("meteor", scope).where(…).rows()            → the admitted rows
  update   service     engine.allowUpdate(permissions, "meteor", patch, bag)    → Verdict on the columns
                       engine.resolveUpdate(permissions, "meteor", bag)        → Scope<"meteor", "update">
           repository  gateDb.update("meteor", scope, id, patch)               → the row, or null
  create   repository  gateDb.create("meteor", permissions, values)            → the row, or null

reference.statement: `index.ts` exports what a caller needs, and nothing that would let one forge or skip a decision.

claims.text: The brand symbol. A `Scope` is a type carrying it, and only `engine.ts` casts a value to that type, so a scope cannot be built anywhere else.
The role walk. Callers get `resolveEffectivePermissions(roles, bag)`; the forest search behind it is internal.
Path resolution and operator compilation. A caller hands over a bag and reads back a scope or a verdict; how `$session.user.id` is walked and how `has` becomes SQL stays in the engine.
`assertNoIssues`, the helper `config.ts` uses to turn a validator's issues into a boot error.
